title: Student Rating Measurement Specification
paragraphs: Appendix H Student Rating Measurement Specication The external human measure is the full published NMLS (Koc & Barut, 2016). Its agent-administered form is an exploratory synthetic diagnostic, not the primary computational outcome or a validated measure of agent competence. Administration uses its authorised item wording and ve-point agreement anchors, not paraphrases of the domain descriptions in this thesis. This appendix provides the scoring map, not a replacement administration form. A translated or shortened instrument has a separate version identity and cannot inherit validity merely by retaining the NMLS name. Table H.1: NMLS Item Map and Student Rating Outputs Domain Published item positions Output FC 17 Mean of 7 responses CC 818 Mean of 11 responses FP 1925 Mean of 7 responses CP 2635 Mean of 10 responses Full-item display 135 100(T −35)/140 Note. Domain means remain on the original 15 scale. The optional 0100 display is this study's linear presentation of the full-item sum; it is not a pass mark, rank threshold, or independent validity claim. The machine-readable column names are NMLS01 through NMLS35. the Student Rating scoring procedure requires all 35 valid integer responses before producing a complete prole; incomplete assessments remain missing, not zero. Completecase scoring does not justify ignoring attrition in the study analysis. Entity type, 296

APPENDIX H. STUDENT RATING MEASUREMENT SPECIFICATION 297 research ID, group, condition, timepoint, language, and instrument version remain attached to each prole, so human observations cannot be pooled silently with synthetic outputs. Model-run identiers identify replication units separately from individual agent IDs. NMLS, task performance, PB, stars, BRS, and platform tier are stored as separate elds. The scoring code checks arithmetic and input integrity; it does not establish a factor model, linguistic equivalence, or agent validity.
